text: Write the Strategy pattern: an algorithm as an object, chosen by the constructor. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: interface Scheduler { int next(int box, int grade); }
int review(int p, int g) { return ___; }
answer: private final Scheduler scheduler|this.scheduler = scheduler|scheduler.next(p, g)
explanation: Verified: 3 then 2. Same class, same call, different answer — and the only difference is the constructor argument. That is what "the caller chooses the policy" means concretely, and it is why `Deck` never calls `new` on a scheduler: doing so would tie it to one policy and make the class untestable without that policy's behaviour.
